result:
Verification passed and the `url-slugs` run is now marked **done**. The one real issue: the slug collision the design warned about happens, and nothing in this change prevents it.

| Item | Result | Evidence (commands actually run) | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **AC1:** `tests/test.sh` passes (lowercases, turns runs of non-alphanumerics into `-`, trims) | pass | `bash tests/test.sh` exited 0 with all 3 checks ok. Running `src/slugify.sh` on 4 sample titles also exited 0 each time. | Verified (multi-source) |
| **FS1:** titles that differ only in punctuation get the same slug | pass | `bash tests/fs1.sh` exited 0: both `Hello, World` and `Hello World` became `hello-world` | Verified (single-source) |

Syntax checks (`bash -n`) on all three scripts also exited 0. Overall confidence is **Verified (single-source)**, the lowest across the items. There's no browser, API, database or logs in this repo to test. shellcheck isn't installed, so no linter ran.

**Regression risk: Low.** The change adds a new, self-contained script that nothing else calls yet, and no shared code changed. The run has no plan, so there was no risk list to check this against.

**Before you use this in production:**
- **Punctuation-only differences collide.** FS1 "passing" means the collision really happens. The design leaves the fix to a later "uniqueness layer", which isn't built. Anything that stores articles by slug will overwrite one with the other.
- **Punctuation-only titles give an empty slug.** For example, `***` produces an empty string. No acceptance criterion covers this.
- **Accented and other non-ASCII letters are dropped.** The design already notes this; I didn't test it.

The report is at `.feature-flow/url-slugs/verify.md`, with the command output saved in `.feature-flow/url-slugs/evidence/`. The knowledge base is turned off, so nothing was captured to it.
